summary: Same 2D pond-ripple simulation and palette on both sides, and the drops even land at the same places at nearly the same times, but the port's wave front travels ~2.5x too fast, its drop impulse is ~3x too weak, and its ripples gain rather than lose energy, so the original's calm dark pond with bright white-blue splashes renders as continuously boiling teal noise.
observations: Both sides render, compile clean, no runtime errors, both steady over a 240 s survey (orig brightnessTrend steady, port steady). No mode/regime structure on either side at 60 s or 240 s; the pattern is one continuous regime, so a late-window check (--skip 200, steady-late) shows the same relationship as t=0.

Shared algorithm skeleton: 16x16 default grid, border ring (x=0, x=15, y=0, y=15) pinned to the exact rest colour (0,~20,22) on BOTH sides; the wave lives on alternating frames at any given pixel (px(6,14) is non-rest only on even frame indices on both sides), i.e. both do the same one-sublattice-per-frame update. Both are resolution-fixed the same way: re-rendered at --grid 8x8 and --grid 32x32 the imagery stays the same blocky logical canvas on both sides, mean brightness unchanged (orig 12, port 13-14 at every grid size).

Drop schedule/placement agrees closely. On a cold start at sliderRaindrops=0 both sides put their first drop at exactly pixel (6,14); orig peaks there at t=0.10, port at t=0.30 (a ~0.2-0.3 s startup lag, and the port sits at flat rest for its first 0.20 s while the orig already has a drop at t=0.00).

DROP IMPULSE AMPLITUDE: original's splash pixel reaches luminance 189-234 (amplitude ~167-212 above the rest level of 22) essentially every time — 29 frames out of 200 in a 10 s untouched window had a peak >150. Port's cold-start splash reaches only 79 (amplitude 57), and in the same 10 s untouched window only 4 of 200 frames had any pixel >150. The bright white-blue droplet flashes that punctuate the original are effectively absent from the port.

WAVE SPEED: measured as the outermost radius with |v-rest|>5 from the single cold-start drop at (6,14), dial=0. Orig: r=1.0 at 0.05 s, 3.2 at 0.50 s, 5.0 at 0.95 s, 6.4 at 1.15 s, front gone by 1.20 s -> ~5.6 px/s. Port: r=1.0 at 0.25 s, 5.1 at 0.50 s, 10.8 at 0.95 s, 13.6 at 1.15 s (already off the 14-px interior) -> ~14.3 px/s. Port's ripple expands about 2.5x too fast.

DAMPING / ENERGY: total field energy E = sum over the 14x14 interior of |v-22|, same single-drop cold start. Orig: E peaks at 222 on the impact frame (t=0.10) and monotonically decays — 133 at 0.20 s, 115 at 0.80 s, 64 at 1.35 s (halved in ~1 s), water back at rest. Port: E climbs from 22 at 0.20 s to 385 at 0.50 s, 560 at 0.80 s, plateaus ~550, and is still 430 at 1.35 s. The port's ripple gets BRIGHTER and BROADER as it expands instead of fading, and the reflected energy keeps rattling around the box.

Net steady-state agitation: over 10 s untouched, mean |v-rest| across the interior is 2.6 for the orig vs 9.1 for the port (3.5x), and the fraction of interior pixels within +/-5 of rest is 88.7% orig vs 46.9% port. The original is mostly still water with one or two live rings; the port has no quiet water anywhere.

Over a 60 s run at sliderRaindrops=0 sampled once per second, orig field deviation averages ~1.5 (range 0.3-3.3) while the port averages ~6.7 (range 0-11.6). Neither diverges or dies — the port simply settles at a ~4.4x hotter equilibrium.

Drop RATE on the original scales cleanly with the dial (isolated-impulse count over 15 s at 20 fps): 1.53 drops/s at sliderRaindrops=0, ~2.9 drops/s untouched, 10.4 drops/s at sliderRaindrops=1. Original impulse peak stays pinned at 189-212 across the whole dial range — the dial changes rate, not brightness.

COLOR matches well and is not a finding: rest = (0,~20,22) dark teal on both; mid ripples average (0,43,70) orig vs (11,52,68) port; peak splash (118,163,216) orig vs (130,192,195) port. Only nit: the port pushes into the red channel more often because its amplitudes are hotter — meanR avg 0.0-0.1 (orig) vs 0.4-2.3 (port) depending on window.

motion stat (whole-rig, 20 fps): orig 2, port 6 untouched; at 240 s / 5 fps orig 4, port 13.6. motion and motionLit agree throughout (dense pattern, not sparse), and zeroMotionFrames is ~0 on both — neither side is frozen.

Frame-rate coupling: rendering the same 20 s window at 10/20/40 fps, the motion stat halves as fps doubles on BOTH sides (orig 3/2/1, port 9/6/3) and mean field deviation is essentially fps-flat on both (orig 4.16/2.51/2.47, port 14.35/9.88/9.97). Both engines are time-based in the same way; the port/orig energy ratio is 3.4-4.0x at every rate, so the divergence is not an fps artefact.
Seed-independent: at --seed 7 and --seed 1234 the relationship is identical (orig motion 2, port motion 6 in both), so this is not a one-seed fluke.
Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, name sliderRaindrops, kind slider, label "Raindrops".

dials.name: sliderRaindrops
dials.origEffect: Rate knob for how often drops fall; drop brightness is unaffected. Measured drop rate 1.53/s at 0, ~2.9/s untouched, 10.4/s at 1. Mean interior field deviation over a 20 s window: 1.58 (v=0), 1.77 (0.25), 2.20 (0.5), 3.29 (0.75), 6.55 (1.0). Peak splash luminance stays 173-198 at every setting. Even at v=1 the water still shows quiet gaps between rings.
dials.portEffect: Same axis and same direction, but shifted about one full dial position hotter and compressed. Mean interior field deviation: 7.28 (v=0), 8.02 (0.25), 9.42 (0.5), 12.14 (0.75), 20.44 (1.0) — i.e. the port at v=0 (7.28) is already hotter than the original at v=1 (6.55), and the whole sweep spans 2.8x where the original spans 4.1x. Peak luminance rises with the dial on the port (100 at v=0 up to 226 at v=1) instead of staying constant.

feedback: Slow the ripple propagation by roughly 2.5x. Measured on the default 16x16 grid from a single cold-start drop at (6,14) with sliderRaindrops=0: the original's outermost disturbed radius (|v-rest|>5) reaches 3.2 px at 0.50 s, 5.0 px at 0.95 s and 6.4 px at 1.15 s (~5.6 px/s); the port reaches 5.1, 10.8 and 13.6 px at the same instants (~14.3 px/s). Target: front radius ~6 px at 1.1 s, wave gone from the 14-px interior by ~1.2 s.

Raise the drop impulse amplitude by about 3x. The original deposits a splash pixel at luminance 189-234 (amplitude ~170-210 above the rest level of 22) on essentially every drop, and that amplitude is independent of the dial. The port's splash tops out around 79 at sliderRaindrops=0 and only reaches ~226 when the dial is cranked to 1 (where the whole field is also overdriven). The visible consequence: the original shows discrete near-white/pale-blue droplet flashes about 3 times a second, the port has none.

Fix the energy balance — the port's ripple GAINS energy as it expands. Sum of |v-rest| over the 14x14 interior after a single drop: original 222 on the impact frame then monotone decay to 64 by 1.35 s; port 22 -> 385 (0.50 s) -> 560 (0.80 s) -> still 430 at 1.35 s. Whatever damping/decay term is applied per step is far too weak (and the amplitude appears to be renormalised outward rather than conserved). Target: peak energy on the impact frame, then a half-life of about 1 second.

Success metric for a fix, measurable straight from a --dump: on the default 16x16 grid, untouched controls, over any 10 s window at 20 fps, at least ~85% of the 14x14 interior pixels should be within +/-5 of the rest level at any instant, and mean |v-rest| should be ~2.5 (the port currently posts 47% and 9.1).

Rebalance the dial mapping after the physics is fixed. The port's whole sliderRaindrops range sits about one dial position hot: its v=0 field energy (7.28) already exceeds the original's v=1 (6.55). Once damping and wave speed are right, re-check that v=0 gives ~1.5 drops/s and v=1 gives ~10 drops/s with the water still returning to rest between rings at v=1.
Minor: the port sits at flat rest for its first ~0.2-0.3 s before its first drop, while the original drops at t=0.00. Same location (6,14), just a startup lag — cosmetic, fix last if at all.

Minor: the port's peak splash colour is (130,192,195) against the original's (118,163,216) — the port's brightest point is slightly green-cyan where the original's is blue-white. Only worth touching once the amplitude fix lands, since the port currently almost never reaches that part of the ramp.

Do NOT change: the border-pinned rest ring, the alternate-frame (checkerboard sublattice) update cadence, the rest colour (0,20,22), the mid-ripple palette, the drop placement/schedule generator, and the fixed-logical-canvas behaviour across grid sizes — all of these already match the original exactly.
